claims.claim: In Python, every object has an identity, a type, and a value; its type determines supported operations.
A Python class creates a new type from which instances can be made.
Python's tutorial presents inheritance as a mechanism in which a derived class can inherit attributes and methods from a base class.
Encapsulation is a design choice that groups an object's related state and behavior behind an interface; Python conventions such as underscore names are not access-control barriers.
Polymorphism means code can use a common operation while different object types provide behavior appropriate to their type; it need not require inheritance.
Composition—having one object use another—is often an alternative to modeling a relationship with inheritance.
